QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_48

question.text: Himalaya Opportunities Fund (Cat II) has called INR 800 crore and distributed INR 1,440 crore to LPs with residual NAV of INR 160 crore. What is the fund's DPI (Distributions to Paid-In)?

explanation.text: The Logic: DPI = Cumulative Distributions to LPs / Paid-in Capital = INR 1,440 / INR 800 = 1.8x, matching keyed option A. Workbook pp.152-154 define DPI as cumulative distributions divided by paid-in capital, with TVPI = DPI + RVPI = (1,440 + 160) / 800 = 2.0x until final exit. The Trap: 2.0x is TVPI (includes residual NAV), not DPI. 0.2x is RVPI alone. 1.4x is wrong arithmetic. Note: A simple sanity check: TVPI always equals DPI plus RVPI, so once a fund is fully realised and RVPI falls to zero, DPI and TVPI must coincide.
